name: The International Academy of Cytology Yokohama System for Reporting Breast Fine Needle Aspiration Biopsy Cytopathology
specimen: Breast FNA (palpation or image-guided), including axillary tail lesions
use: All breast FNA specimens (palpable and image-guided).
Interpret alongside clinical examination and imaging (triple test).
not_use: Nipple discharge and nipple scrape cytology (report descriptively).
Core needle biopsy histology (use histological B-categories, e.g. UK B1–B5).
report_structure: Specimen, side, site (clock position), guidance, lesion size and imaging category (BI-RADS) if available
Comment: triple-test correlation and recommended next step
terminology: Use 'Carcinoma, consistent with ductal carcinoma NST' (or 'Malignant – carcinoma') on cytology; avoid 'invasive', 'infiltrating' and 'IDC' because invasion cannot be assessed on FNA.
DCIS cannot be distinguished from invasive carcinoma on FNA.

adequacy.title: Adequacy principles
items: No numerical threshold; adequacy depends on whether the material allows a confident diagnosis in the context of the clinical and imaging findings.
Rapid on-site evaluation (ROSE) reduces insufficient rates.
Specimens with atypical/suspicious/malignant cells are never 'Insufficient'.
Benign cyst fluid with resolution of cyst on imaging may be reported as Benign; fat alone is insufficient unless concordant with lipoma.

categories.name: Insufficient / Inadequate
categories.definition: Material is too scant, too poorly preserved or obscured to allow a cytological diagnosis; judged relative to the clinical/imaging lesion.
categories.management: Repeat FNA (preferably image-guided) or core needle biopsy, guided by triple-test (clinical + imaging) findings.
criteria: Insufficient epithelial cells for diagnosis in a solid lesion (no fixed number; experience-based judgement).
Poor fixation/air-drying, crush, thick smears, obscuring blood.
Cyst fluid with only macrophages and no epithelium – may be 'Benign' if imaging shows simple cyst that resolved; otherwise Insufficient.
Fat only from a mass lesion is insufficient unless clinically/radiologically a lipoma.

diagnoses.name: Insufficient – scant/acellular material
diagnoses.final: Insufficient/Inadequate (IAC Yokohama Category 1). The material is insufficient for cytological diagnosis.
diagnoses.comment: Correlate with clinical and imaging findings (triple test). Repeat image-guided FNA or core biopsy is recommended.

diagnoses.name: Insufficient – artefact/obscured
diagnoses.final: Insufficient/Inadequate (IAC Yokohama Category 1) due to air-drying/crush artefact/obscuring blood.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat FNA/core biopsy recommended.

diagnoses.name: Insufficient – cyst fluid only (non-concordant imaging)
diagnoses.final: Insufficient/Inadequate (IAC Yokohama Category 1). Cyst contents with macrophages only; no epithelial cells.
diagnoses.comment: If imaging shows a complex cyst or residual mass, repeat FNA/core biopsy of the solid component is recommended.

categories.name: Benign
categories.definition: Clearly benign cytological features, with a specific diagnosis where possible.
categories.management: If triple test concordant benign: clinical/imaging follow-up. If not concordant: core biopsy.
criteria: Moderate cellularity of cohesive flat sheets of ductal cells with myoepithelial cells, bare bipolar nuclei in background.
Specific patterns: fibroadenoma (staghorn sheets, fibromyxoid stroma, bipolar nuclei), fat necrosis, mastitis, lactational change, cyst with apocrine cells, gynaecomastia.
No significant atypia, no dyscohesion beyond expected.

diagnoses.name: Fibroadenoma
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Consistent with fibroadenoma.
diagnoses.comment: Cellular aspirate with branching (staghorn) cohesive sheets with myoepithelial cells, numerous bare bipolar nuclei and fibromyxoid stromal fragments. Correlate with triple test.

diagnoses.name: Fibrocystic change (incl. apocrine metaplasia, cyst)
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Fibrocystic change.
diagnoses.comment: Benign ductal cells, apocrine cells, foamy macrophages and cyst fluid.

diagnoses.name: Benign cyst
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Consistent with benign cyst.
diagnoses.comment: Correlate with imaging; aspirate residual mass if present.

diagnoses.name: Fat necrosis
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Consistent with fat necrosis.
diagnoses.comment: Foamy/lipid-laden macrophages, multinucleated giant cells and degenerated fat. History of trauma/surgery supports; correlate with imaging.

diagnoses.name: Acute mastitis / breast abscess
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Acute inflammation/abscess.
diagnoses.comment: Neutrophils and debris; culture advised; follow up to resolution to exclude inflammatory carcinoma.

diagnoses.name: Subareolar abscess / duct ectasia / periductal mastitis
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Features of subareolar abscess (anucleate squames, keratin, inflammation) / duct ectasia.
diagnoses.comment: Correlate clinically.

diagnoses.name: Granulomatous mastitis (idiopathic/tuberculous)
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Granulomatous mastitis.
diagnoses.comment: Epithelioid granulomas ± necrosis. ZN stain/AFB culture/CBNAAT recommended to exclude tuberculosis; idiopathic granulomatous lobular mastitis in differential.

diagnoses.name: Lactational change / lactating adenoma
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Lactational change.
diagnoses.comment: Cells with vacuolated cytoplasm, prominent nucleoli and proteinaceous background; pregnancy/lactation history required.

diagnoses.name: Gynaecomastia
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Consistent with gynaecomastia.
diagnoses.comment: Cohesive ductal sheets with bipolar nuclei in a male breast.

diagnoses.name: Intramammary lymph node
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Reactive lymphoid cells consistent with intramammary lymph node.
diagnoses.comment: Polymorphous lymphoid cells with tingible-body macrophages and no epithelial cells. Correlate with imaging (reniform node with fatty hilum).

diagnoses.name: Lipoma / benign adipose tissue (concordant)
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Mature adipose tissue, consistent with lipoma in the clinical/radiological context.
diagnoses.comment: Fat alone is considered Insufficient if imaging suggests a solid non-fatty lesion.

diagnoses.name: Benign proliferative breast disease without atypia
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Proliferative breast disease without atypia.
diagnoses.comment: Cellular cohesive sheets with streaming and myoepithelial cells; usual ductal hyperplasia/papilloma may be within this pattern.

diagnoses.name: Benign skin adnexal cyst (epidermal inclusion cyst)
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Contents of epidermal inclusion cyst.
diagnoses.comment: Anucleate squames and keratinous debris ± foreign-body giant cells; ruptured cysts can cause reactive atypia.

diagnoses.name: Silicone/foreign-body reaction
diagnoses.final: Benign (IAC Yokohama Category 2). Foreign-body (silicone) reaction.
diagnoses.comment: Vacuolated histiocytes and giant cells with refractile non-birefringent material; correlate with implant history.

categories.name: Atypical
categories.definition: Cytological features that are mainly benign but with some features seen uncommonly in benign lesions and that may be seen in malignancy; or features of a lesion with uncertain behaviour.
categories.management: Core needle biopsy (preferred) or repeat FNA; manage per triple test.
criteria: Benign pattern with mild atypia, loss of cohesion, or increased cellularity.
Papillary lesion without atypia (fibrovascular cores, columnar cells) – papilloma vs papillary carcinoma uncertain.
Fibroepithelial lesion with cellular stroma (fibroadenoma vs phyllodes).
Mucinous lesion with scant atypia (mucocele-like lesion vs mucinous carcinoma).
Columnar cell lesions/atypical ductal hyperplasia-like patterns; low cellularity atypical cells.

diagnoses.name: Atypical – papillary lesion
diagnoses.final: Atypical (IAC Yokohama Category 3). Papillary lesion.
diagnoses.comment: Papillary fragments with fibrovascular cores and columnar cells; papilloma cannot be distinguished from papillary carcinoma on cytology. Core biopsy recommended.

diagnoses.name: Atypical – fibroepithelial lesion with cellular stroma (fibroadenoma vs phyllodes)
diagnoses.final: Atypical (IAC Yokohama Category 3). Fibroepithelial lesion; phyllodes tumour cannot be excluded.
diagnoses.comment: Hypercellular stromal fragments with spindle cells. Core biopsy/excision recommended.

diagnoses.name: Atypical – mucinous lesion
diagnoses.final: Atypical (IAC Yokohama Category 3). Mucinous lesion.
diagnoses.comment: Mucin with few bland epithelial cells; differential includes mucocele-like lesion and mucinous carcinoma. Core biopsy recommended.

diagnoses.name: Atypical – epithelial cells with mild atypia
diagnoses.final: Atypical (IAC Yokohama Category 3). Atypical ductal epithelial cells.
diagnoses.comment: Benign versus low-grade neoplasia (e.g. ADH/low-grade DCIS/low-grade carcinoma) cannot be resolved; core biopsy recommended.

diagnoses.name: Atypical – low cellularity with atypia
diagnoses.final: Atypical (IAC Yokohama Category 3). Few atypical cells.
diagnoses.comment: Insufficient for a definite diagnosis; repeat FNA/core biopsy recommended.

diagnoses.name: Atypical – atypical apocrine cells
diagnoses.final: Atypical (IAC Yokohama Category 3). Atypical apocrine cells.
diagnoses.comment: Apocrine atypia may be reactive (e.g. in sclerosing adenosis) or neoplastic; core biopsy suggested.

diagnoses.name: Atypical – granular cell tumour / spindle cell lesion
diagnoses.final: Atypical (IAC Yokohama Category 3). Spindle cell lesion / granular cells.
diagnoses.comment: Includes granular cell tumour, myofibroblastoma, fibromatosis, nodular fasciitis; core biopsy for IHC.

diagnoses.name: Atypical – radial scar/complex sclerosing lesion pattern
diagnoses.final: Atypical (IAC Yokohama Category 3).
diagnoses.comment: Cytology cannot reliably distinguish from tubular carcinoma; core biopsy recommended.

categories.name: Suspicious of malignancy
categories.definition: Features suggestive of, but not diagnostic of, malignancy (quantity or quality insufficient), or specific lesions where only histology can confirm.
categories.management: Core needle biopsy (or excision) before definitive treatment.
criteria: Moderate atypia in a dyscohesive population lacking myoepithelial cells, but insufficient for malignancy.
Suspicious of low-grade carcinoma (lobular, tubular, low-grade NST).

diagnoses.name: Suspicious of malignancy – carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious of malignancy (IAC Yokohama Category 4). Suspicious of carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Atypical dyscohesive epithelial cells, quantitatively/qualitatively insufficient for a definitive malignant diagnosis. Core biopsy recommended.

diagnoses.name: Suspicious – lobular carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious of malignancy (IAC Yokohama Category 4). Suspicious of lobular carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Small monotonous single cells/linear files with intracytoplasmic lumina; core biopsy with E-cadherin recommended.

diagnoses.name: Suspicious – low-grade/tubular carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious of malignancy (IAC Yokohama Category 4). Suspicious of low-grade carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Angular tubules with minimal atypia and absent myoepithelial cells. Core biopsy recommended.

diagnoses.name: Suspicious – papillary carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious of malignancy (IAC Yokohama Category 4). Papillary lesion, suspicious of papillary carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Core biopsy/excision recommended.

diagnoses.name: Suspicious – mucinous carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious of malignancy (IAC Yokohama Category 4). Mucinous lesion suspicious of mucinous carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Abundant mucin with atypical epithelial clusters but insufficient for definitive diagnosis; core biopsy recommended.

categories.name: Malignant
categories.definition: Unequivocal malignant features; specify type where possible. Do not use 'invasive'/'infiltrating' on cytology because invasion cannot be assessed.
categories.management: If triple test concordant malignant: definitive management may proceed per local policy, but core biopsy is generally recommended for histological type, grade and biomarkers (ER/PR/HER2/Ki-67).
criteria: Usually cellular, dyscohesive population of atypical epithelial cells, absent bipolar nuclei/myoepithelial cells.
Nuclear enlargement, pleomorphism, irregular chromatin, nucleoli; necrosis in high-grade.
Specific types: lobular, mucinous, papillary, medullary-like, metaplastic, apocrine, secretory, adenoid cystic, lymphoma, metastasis, sarcoma/malignant phyllodes.

diagnoses.name: Carcinoma, consistent with ductal carcinoma NST
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Carcinoma, consistent with ductal carcinoma of no special type (NST).
diagnoses.comment: Cellular dyscohesive pleomorphic malignant epithelial cells with absent myoepithelial cells. In-situ versus invasive disease cannot be determined on cytology. Core biopsy for histological type, grade and ER/PR/HER2/Ki-67 is recommended.

diagnoses.name: Lobular carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Carcinoma, consistent with lobular carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Dyscohesive small monotonous cells with intracytoplasmic lumina/signet-ring forms. Core biopsy with E-cadherin and biomarkers recommended.

diagnoses.name: Mucinous carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Carcinoma, consistent with mucinous carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Abundant extracellular mucin with clusters of mildly atypical cells and capillary fragments.

diagnoses.name: Papillary carcinoma (encapsulated/solid/invasive)
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Papillary carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Histology needed to determine encapsulated/solid papillary or invasive status.

diagnoses.name: Carcinoma with medullary features / triple-negative high-grade
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). High-grade carcinoma (NST) with medullary-like features.
diagnoses.comment: Syncytial sheets of large pleomorphic cells with lymphocytes; biomarkers on core.

diagnoses.name: Metaplastic carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Malignant neoplasm, consistent with metaplastic carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Squamous/spindle/matrix-producing components; CK (incl. p63/CK5/6) on core needed.

diagnoses.name: Apocrine carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Carcinoma with apocrine features.
diagnoses.comment: AR+/GCDFP-15+ on core.

diagnoses.name: Secretory carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Carcinoma, consistent with secretory carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: ETV6::NTRK3 fusion; pan-TRK IHC on core.

diagnoses.name: Adenoid cystic carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Carcinoma consistent with adenoid cystic carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Basaloid cells with hyaline globules; MYB on core.

diagnoses.name: Malignant phyllodes tumour / primary sarcoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Malignant spindle cell neoplasm (malignant phyllodes tumour vs sarcoma vs metaplastic carcinoma).
diagnoses.comment: Core biopsy/excision with IHC required.

diagnoses.name: Angiosarcoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Malignant vascular neoplasm, suggestive of angiosarcoma.
diagnoses.comment: Bloody aspirate with atypical spindle/epithelioid cells; CD31/ERG on core; history of radiotherapy relevant.

diagnoses.name: Lymphoma of breast
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
diagnoses.comment: Flow cytometry/IHC; BIA-ALCL (CD30+, ALK−) in implant seroma.

diagnoses.name: Metastatic tumour to breast (melanoma, lung, ovary, etc.)
diagnoses.final: Malignant (IAC Yokohama Category 5). Metastatic [type].
diagnoses.comment: IHC and clinical history needed.

extra.title: Triple test
items: Clinical + imaging + cytology. Concordant benign → follow-up; any discordance → core biopsy/excision.
Malignant FNA with concordant clinical/imaging can support treatment planning, but most centres still obtain core biopsy for receptors.

references: Field AS, Raymond WA, Schmitt F (eds). The International Academy of Cytology Yokohama System for Reporting Breast Fine Needle Aspiration Biopsy Cytopathology. Springer, 2020.
Field AS, Raymond WA, Rickard M, et al. The International Academy of Cytology Yokohama System for Reporting Breast Fine-Needle Aspiration Biopsy Cytopathology. Acta Cytol. 2019;63(4):257–273.
WHO Classification of Tumours Editorial Board. Breast Tumours. 5th ed. IARC, 2019.
